## Overview This PR moves GLM-5.3-Flash's KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) layers onto FlashInfer kernels: - the fused single-token decode (`fused_kda_decode`); - the packed multi-token decode for draft-verify rows (`packed_fused_kda_decode`); - optionally, the CuTe DSL chunked prefill (`recurrent_kda(backend="cute-dsl")`). Kimi K3 already uses these kernels through the same `vllm.utils.flashinfer` wrappers and the same `kda_decode_backend` / `kda_spec_decode_backend` / `kda_prefill_backend` options. The model has 34 KDA layers (64 heads of 128). Today each decode step runs three Triton kernels per layer, and mixed steps send their decode rows through the chunked prefill kernel. - **Decode:** default `auto`; activates where FlashInfer supports the layer. - **Prefill:** opt-in `--kda-prefill-backend flashinfer`. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Requires FlashInfer 0.7.3.** This PR assumes the FlashInfer pin bump to 0.7.3 (a separate PR) has landed. > 0.7.3 contains flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7132 (16/64 heads in `fused_kda_decode` / `packed_fused_kda_decode`, and > the DS conv-state layout) and #6201 (SM107 prefill). GLM-5.3-Flash's 64-head (TP1 / DP attention) and 16-head > (TP4) ranks, and the DS layout that NIXL P/D needs, rely on #7132. With the current pin (0.7.2.post1) the static > support checks accept configurations that 0.7.2 rejects at its first call, so this PR should merge after the bump. ## Claims - **Decode kernels** (VR200, 34 layers per step, CUDA graph, L2 flushed): - 1.9–2.1x faster at 1–8 rows per GPU; - 1.3–1.8x faster at 32–512 rows (H64 fp32 at 512 rows: 19.5 → 12.4 ms per step; H64 bf16: 16.2 → 9.2 ms); - pure decode steps run in a FULL CUDA graph (`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, KDA captured), so the GPU times above are what serving pays; in eager (PIECEWISE, mixed/prefill) steps the host enqueue also drops, 3.0 → 0.95 ms per 34 layers. - **Mixed prefill + decode steps** (one layer, H64): 46–61% faster (32K prefill tokens + 512 decode rows: 6.96 → 2.72 ms). Most of it is the decode-row peel. - **FlashInfer prefill (opt-in):** 8–12% per layer at 4+ long sequences; 3–8% slower in eager steps with 1 sequence at H64 or a few at H16, mostly from the call's host time (about 95 µs vs FlashKDA's 18 µs on VR200, where FlashInfer's kernel is faster). This is why it stays opt-in. - **Serving on GB300 and GB200**, native srt-slurm sa-bench 8K/1K, Dynamo, base vs this PR (+ the FlashInfer change): - agg DEP2 (64 KDA heads per rank): +13.7% / +24.9% TPS/GPU on GB300 at C512 / C1024 (2847 → 3237, 2402 → 2999); +13.5% / +14.8% on GB200, which is KV-capacity bound; - disagg with the DS conv layout via NIXL, C512: +5.1% (GB300) and +6.0% (GB200) TPS/GPU; - agg TP4 (16 heads per rank): +1.4–3.0% at C1–C32. - **Where it comes from:** decode steps run one fused FlashInfer kernel per layer instead of three Triton kernels, and mixed steps send their decode rows to that kernel instead of the chunked prefill kernel (the decode-row peel). - **FlashInfer prefill (opt-in):** faster for several long sequences per step; slower for one or a few sequences at low concurrency, mostly from the call's host time (Follow-ups). Reference from earlier VR200 work: 91.40%. ### MTP (speculative decoding, 2 draft tokens) GSM8K 40-shot as above with `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'`, agg DEP2, VR200, nightly c50aca14. Covers the draft-verify path (`packed_fused_kda_decode`) and prefill/decode with spec-decoding metadata. | Arm | Runs | Mean | Draft acceptance (accepted / drafted tokens, both runs) | |---|---|---|---| | base (nightly c50aca14) | 92.27, 91.89 | 92.08 | 88.6% (162475 / 183370) | | this PR, decode + prefill on FlashInfer | 91.21, 91.89 | 91.55 | 88.7% (160379 / 180818) | Accuracy is within the ±1-point spread of greedy runs seen above, and draft acceptance is unchanged. The PR arm's logs show the FlashInfer prefill and the packed decode (3 tokens per row) in use. Serving with MTP (sa-bench 8K/1K random, agg DEP2, C128 and C256, VR200) also completed every request in both arms, with the same draft acceptance. This check found a bug in an earlier revision: under speculative decoding the builder's non-spec slot indices are a strided column of the [N, 1 + num_spec] block table, which FlashInfer's prefill rejects. Warmup failed with `ValueError: backend='cute-dsl' does not support this recurrent_kda prefill contract`. The prefill now passes contiguous indices, and a unit test covers it. ### Serving (GB300 and GB200) Native srt-slurm sa-bench, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, random data, Dynamo frontend, on Lyris (GB300 and GB200, 4 GPUs per node). Settings: - `max-num-batched-tokens` 32768; - fp8 KV; - FlashInfer TRT-LLM NVFP4 MoE; - SD conv layout for agg, DS for disagg. Base: nightly 8e2beaa3. PR: the same image + this branch's `kda.py` + the final flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7132 files, with `--kda-prefill-backend flashinfer`. Single runs; all points completed every request. The same recipes were also run on VR200. | GPU | Config | C | Base TPS/GPU | PR TPS/GPU | Δ | Base tok/s/user | PR tok/s/user | Base TPOT ms | PR TPOT ms | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | GB300 | agg DEP2 (2 GPU) | 512 | 2847 | 3237 | +13.7% | 11.13 | 12.66 | 82.75 | 71.48 | | GB300 | agg DEP2 (2 GPU) | 1024 | 2402 | 2999 | +24.9% | 4.76 | 5.93 | 158.91 | 133.83 | | GB300 | agg TP4 (4 GPU) | 1 | 54.7 | 55.4 | +1.4% | 218.66 | 221.66 | 4.44 | 4.36 | | GB300 | agg TP4 (4 GPU) | 8 | 299.4 | 307.3 | +2.6% | 149.73 | 153.68 | 6.10 | 5.88 | | GB300 | agg TP4 (4 GPU) | 32 | 678.4 | 692.0 | +2.0% | 84.84 | 86.53 | 10.36 | 10.10 | | GB300 | 4P(TP1)+1D(DEP4) (8 GPU), DS layout | 512 | 2657 | 2793 | +5.1% | 43.02 | 45.27 | 20.74 | 19.18 | | GB200 | agg DEP2 (2 GPU) | 512 | 2090 | 2372 | +13.5% | 8.41 | 9.52 | 61.91 | 64.22 | | GB200 | agg DEP2 (2 GPU) | 1024 | 2100 | 2410 | +14.8% | 4.26 | 4.87 | 62.30 | 64.05 | | GB200 | agg TP4 (4 GPU) | 1 | 53.1 | 54.7 | +3.0% | 212.47 | 218.90 | 4.57 | 4.41 | | GB200 | agg TP4 (4 GPU) | 8 | 294.7 | 302.8 | +2.8% | 147.38 | 151.45 | 6.16 | 5.94 | | GB200 | agg TP4 (4 GPU) | 32 | 671.6 | 683.3 | +1.7% | 83.98 | 85.44 | 10.45 | 10.24 | | GB200 | 2P(DEP2)+1D(DEP4) (8 GPU), DS layout | 512 | 2199 | 2330 | +6.0% | 35.73 | 38.03 | 18.58 | 17.63 | - **DEP2 at C1024 with fp32 KDA state** is capacity-bound: the state takes about 142 MB per sequence, so requests queue and every step is a mixed step. The PR's gain there is admission: faster mixed steps cut mean TTFT 58 → 42 s (C512) and 176 → 145 s (C1024), while per-token decode time is slightly higher with the larger running batch. Hence +14.8% at C1024 rather than about +25%. - **GB200 disagg shape:** one GB200 cannot hold the 191 GB checkpoint at TP1, so each prefill worker is DEP2 (TP1 per rank, experts over 2 GPUs). Mixed steps with verify rows keep the Triton spec path. - **Mixed steps without spec rows** run the leading decode rows (vLLM orders decodes first) through the fused kernel. The conv then skips those rows as null slots, so the builder's existing causal-conv metadata stays valid. The prefill kernel uses the builder's prefill tail (`prefill_query_start_loc` / `prefill_state_indices` / `prefill_has_initial_state`), as the GDN layer already does. FlashKDA's prepare kernel thus no longer scans hundreds of one-token sequences, and gather / scatter no longer move their states. With prefix-cache checkpoints the step keeps today's path. - **Selection:** `--kda-decode-backend` (`additional_config.kda_decode_backend`) and `additional_config.kda_spec_decode_backend` take `auto` / `flashinfer` / `triton`. - As for Kimi K3, a static check decides (`_is_flashinfer_kda_decode_supported`): CUDA SM10x, D=128, conv width 4, bf16 activations and conv state, fp32 or bf16 recurrent state, a bounded gate, and the head counts and layouts of FlashInfer with #7132 (single-token rows: 8/12/16/24/32/48/64/96 heads, SD or DS; draft-verify rows: 12–96 heads, SD only, at most 7 draft tokens). - `auto` falls back to Triton when the check fails; `flashinfer` raises. - The prefill opt-in uses the same pattern (`_is_flashinfer_kda_prefill_supported`: SM100 / SM103 / SM107, D=128, bf16 activations, fp32 or bf16 state, bounded gate) and raises at startup when it fails. - **Norm placement:** the fused kernel applies `o_norm`, so with the FlashInfer backend `_forward` returns normed output for every step type. In PIECEWISE (mixed/prefill) steps, breakable CUDA graphs run `_forward` eagerly but the code after it is replayed as captured, so whether to norm must not depend on the step type. **Prefill (opt-in).** - **Call:** `--kda-prefill-backend flashinfer` (already a CLI choice, previously rejected for GLM-5.3) calls `recurrent_kda(backend="cute-dsl")` with the raw gate and beta logits. - **In place:** it reads and writes the recurrent state pool through `ssm_state_indices`, so there is no gather, scatter or final-state buffer. - **Fresh sequences:** FlashInfer has no has-initial-state flag, so their slots are zeroed first with one `index_fill_`; rows with state zero the unused null slot. - **Edge cases:** - a step whose prefill rows total one token uses the recurrent kernel; - steps with verify rows write their own output buffer and need no FlashKDA workspace. - **Opt-in** (as for Kimi K3), and it produces no prefix-cache checkpoints (`kda_prefill_checkpoint_alignment` is None). **Numerics.** FlashInfer's kernels are not bit-identical to Triton/FlashKDA (different summation orders). Against an fp32/fp64 reference they are as close or closer: - decode error equals the Triton path's; - FlashInfer prefill: 4.2e-3 vs FlashKDA 5.1e-3 (max abs error, H64, 8 x 8192 tokens). GSM8K above is the end-to-end check. **Limitations / follow-ups.** - Requires flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7132 (and #6201 for SM107 prefill); bump the FlashInfer pin to the first release that has it before this PR leaves draft. - Host cost (eager PIECEWISE steps only; FULL-graph decode steps do not pay it): FlashInfer's validating decode wrapper costs more per call than its cached kernel launch; a cheaper FlashInfer launch path would help low concurrency. - Not in this PR: a faster prefill conv (planar / TMA output; overlaps vllm-project/vllm#61614), 64-row norm tiles, and a pipelined bf16-state decode kernel. - CI: `tests/models/glm5next` runs on H200 (SM90), where these tests skip or exercise FlashInfer's kernels only where FlashInfer supports them. SM10x coverage needs a Blackwell lane. - Follow-up: few-sequence prefill steps. With `--kda-prefill-backend flashinfer`, TTFT at low concurrency is higher (GB300 TP4: C1 143 → 163 ms, C8 603 → 650 ms). Most of the cost is the prefill call's host time, paid 34 times per eager prefill step: on GB300 about 190 µs on FlashInfer's two-kernel route (2 x sequences x heads <= SMs) and 110 µs on its one-kernel route, vs FlashKDA's 50–56 µs; at 1–4 sequences the kernel is also 7–13% slower than FlashKDA's. A prototype that routes such steps to FlashKDA brings C1 TTFT back to base, with unchanged throughput, but reserves FlashKDA's workspace (less KV cache) and ties the cutover to FlashInfer's routing rule. It is left out of this PR; the host overhead is reported to FlashInfer, whose fix would make it unnecessary. ---

The same recipes were also run on VR200. | GPU | Config | C | Base TPS/GPU | PR TPS/GPU | Δ | Base tok/s/user | PR tok/s/user | Base TPOT ms | PR TPOT ms | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | GB300 | agg DEP2 (2 GPU) | 512 | 2847 | 3237 | +13.7% | 11.13 | 12.66 | 82.75 | 71.48 | | GB300 | agg DEP2 (2 GPU) | 1024 | 2402 | 2999 | +24.9% | 4.76 | 5.93 | 158.91 | 133.83 | | GB300 | agg TP4 (4 GPU) | 1 | 54.7 | 55.4 | +1.4% | 218.66 | 221.66 | 4.44 | 4.36 | | GB300 | agg TP4 (4 GPU) | 8 | 299.4 | 307.3 | +2.6% | 149.73 | 153.68 | 6.10 | 5.88 | | GB300 | agg TP4 (4 GPU) | 32 | 678.4 | 692.0 | +2.0% | 84.84 | 86.53 | 10.36 | 10.10 | | GB300 | 4P(TP1)+1D(DEP4) (8 GPU), DS layout | 512 | 2657 | 2793 | +5.1% | 43.02 | 45.27 | 20.74 | 19.18 | | GB200 | agg DEP2 (2 GPU) | 512 | 2090 | 2372 | +13.5% | 8.41 | 9.52 | 61.91 | 64.22 | | GB200 | agg DEP2 (2 GPU) | 1024 | 2100 | 2410 | +14.8% | 4.26 | 4.87 | 62.30 | 64.05 | | GB200 | agg TP4 (4 GPU) | 1 | 53.1 | 54.7 | +3.0% | 212.47 | 218.90 | 4.57 | 4.41 | | GB200 | agg TP4 (4 GPU) | 8 | 294.7 | 302.8 | +2.8% | 147.38 | 151.45 | 6.16 | 5.94 | | GB200 | agg TP4 (4 GPU) | 32 | 671.6 | 683.3 | +1.7% | 83.98 | 85.44 | 10.45 | 10.24 | | GB200 | 2P(DEP2)+1D(DEP4) (8 GPU), DS layout | 512 | 2199 | 2330 | +6.0% | 35.73 | 38.03 | 18.58 | 17.63 | - **DEP2 at C1024 with fp32 KDA state** is capacity-bound: the state takes about 142 MB per sequence, so requests queue and every step is a mixed step. That is where the decode-row peel pays most. - **TP4 at low concurrency** is decode-bound; KDA is only part of each step, so the per-step gain is a few percent. - **GB200 agg DEP2** is KV-capacity bound (about 186 GB per GPU): TPOT stays at 62–64 ms from C512 to C1024 and requests queue (mean TTFT 58 s for base at C512). The PR's gain there is admission: faster mixed steps cut mean TTFT 58 → 42 s (C512) and 176 → 145 s (C1024), while per-token decode time is slightly higher with the larger running batch. Hence +14.8% at C1024 rather than about +25%. - **GB200 disagg shape:** one GB200 cannot hold the 191 GB checkpoint at TP1, so each prefill worker is DEP2 (TP1 per rank, experts over 2 GPUs). A TP2 prefill does not work with a TP1-per-rank decode for this model: the hybrid KDA block size follows the per-rank KDA state, and NIXL rejects the mismatched blocks (8576 vs 4352). - **TTFT at TP4, C1–C8** is 20–47 ms higher in the PR arm (GB300 C1 143 → 163 ms, C8 603 → 650 ms; GB200 C1 147 → 169 ms, C8 652 → 681 ms). These steps prefill one or a few sequences at 16 heads. On GB300 the FlashInfer prefill call costs about 190 µs of host time vs FlashKDA's 50–56 µs (34 layers per step), and at 1–4 sequences its kernel is also 7–13% slower; this is why the FlashInfer prefill stays opt-in. Decode alone was not run on GB300/GB200. ## Details **Decode.** - **Plain decode steps** call `flashinfer_fused_kda_decode` once per layer: conv + SiLU with the conv-state update, the recurrence, and the gated RMSNorm, writing the layer output buffer. Slot ≤ 0 rows are null rows. - **Draft-verify steps** (MTP) call `flashinfer_packed_fused_kda_decode` with the existing `spec_state_indices_tensor` / `num_accepted_tokens`. Mixed steps with verify rows keep the Triton spec path. - **Mixed steps without spec rows** run the leading decode rows (vLLM orders decodes first) through the fused kernel. The conv then skips those rows as null slots, so the builder's existing causal-conv metadata stays valid. The prefill kernel uses the builder's prefill tail (`prefill_query_start_loc` / `prefill_state_indices` / `prefill_has_initial_state`), as the GDN layer already does. FlashKDA's prepare kernel thus no longer scans hundreds of one-token sequences, and gather / scatter no longer move their states. With prefix-cache checkpoints the step keeps today's path. - **Selection:** `--kda-decode-backend` (`additional_config.kda_decode_backend`) and `additional_config.kda_spec_decode_backend` take `auto` / `flashinfer` / `triton`. - As for Kimi K3, a static check decides (`_is_flashinfer_kda_decode_supported`): CUDA SM10x, D=128, conv width 4, bf16 activations and conv state, fp32 or bf16 recurrent state, a bounded gate, and the head counts and layouts of FlashInfer with #7132 (single-token rows: 8/12/16/24/32/48/64/96 heads, SD or DS; draft-verify rows: 12–96 heads, SD only, at most 7 draft tokens). - `auto` falls back to Triton when the check fails; `flashinfer` raises. - The prefill opt-in uses the same pattern (`_is_flashinfer_kda_prefill_supported`: SM100 / SM103 / SM107, D=128, bf16 activations, fp32 or bf16 state, bounded gate) and raises at startup when it fails. - **Norm placement:** the fused kernel applies `o_norm`, so with the FlashInfer backend `_forward` returns normed output for every step type. In PIECEWISE (mixed/prefill) steps, breakable CUDA graphs run `_forward` eagerly but the code after it is replayed as captured, so whether to norm must not depend on the step type. **Prefill (opt-in).** - **Call:** `--kda-prefill-backend flashinfer` (already a CLI choice, previously rejected for GLM-5.3) calls `recurrent_kda(backend="cute-dsl")` with the raw gate and beta logits. - **In place:** it reads and writes the recurrent state pool through `ssm_state_indices`, so there is no gather, scatter or final-state buffer. - **Fresh sequences:** FlashInfer has no has-initial-state flag, so their slots are zeroed first with one `index_fill_`; rows with state zero the unused null slot. - **Edge cases:** - a step whose prefill rows total one token uses the recurrent kernel; - steps with verify rows write their own output buffer and need no FlashKDA workspace. - **Opt-in** (as for Kimi K3), and it produces no prefix-cache checkpoints (`kda_prefill_checkpoint_alignment` is None). **Numerics.** FlashInfer's kernels are not bit-identical to Triton/FlashKDA (different summation orders). Against an fp32/fp64 reference they are as close or closer: - decode error equals the Triton path's; - FlashInfer prefill: 4.2e-3 vs FlashKDA 5.1e-3 (max abs error, H64, 8 x 8192 tokens). GSM8K above is the end-to-end check. **Limitations / follow-ups.** - Requires flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7132 (and #6201 for SM107 prefill); bump the FlashInfer pin to the first release that has it before this PR leaves draft. - Host cost (eager PIECEWISE steps only; FULL-graph decode steps do not pay it): FlashInfer's validating decode wrapper costs more per call than its cached kernel launch; a cheaper FlashInfer launch path would help low concurrency. - Not in this PR: a faster prefill conv (planar / TMA output; overlaps vllm-project/vllm#61614), 64-row norm tiles, and a pipelined bf16-state decode kernel. - CI: `tests/models/glm5next` runs on H200 (SM90), where these tests skip or exercise FlashInfer's kernels only where FlashInfer supports them. SM10x coverage needs a Blackwell lane. - Follow-up: few-sequence prefill steps. With `--kda-prefill-backend flashinfer`, TTFT at low concurrency is higher (GB300 TP4: C1 143 → 163 ms, C8 603 → 650 ms). Most of the cost is the prefill call's host time, paid 34 times per eager prefill step: on GB300 about 190 µs on FlashInfer's two-kernel route (2 x sequences x heads <= SMs) and 110 µs on its one-kernel route, vs FlashKDA's 50–56 µs; at 1–4 sequences the kernel is also 7–13% slower than FlashKDA's. A prototype that routes such steps to FlashKDA brings C1 TTFT back to base, with unchanged throughput, but reserves FlashKDA's workspace (less KV cache) and ties the cutover to FlashInfer's routing rule. It is left out of this PR; the host overhead is reported to FlashInfer, whose fix would make it unnecessary. ---

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""GLM-5.3-Flash KDA layers on FlashInfer's kernels: the fused decode (conv +
+SiLU, the recurrence and the gated RMSNorm in one launch) and the CuTe DSL
+chunked prefill.
+
+Each test runs the same layer, weights, caches and step once on the Triton
+path FlashInfer replaces and once on FlashInfer: conv states must match
+exactly, recurrent states and outputs within kernel rounding, and null or
+unused slots must stay untouched.
+"""
+
+from math import prod
+from typing import Any
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from transformers import Glm5NextTextConfig
+
+from tests.v1.attention.utils import create_vllm_config
+from vllm.config import SpeculativeConfig, VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+from vllm.forward_context import set_forward_context
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.mamba_utils import get_conv_state_layout
+from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_utils import default_weight_loader
+from vllm.models.glm5next.common.kda import (
+    Glm5NextLinearAttention,
+    _is_flashinfer_kda_prefill_supported,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_default_torch_dtype
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.gdn_attn import GDNAttentionMetadata
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils import compute_causal_conv1d_metadata
+
+if not current_platform.is_cuda():
+    pytest.skip("FlashInfer KDA kernels are CUDA-only", allow_module_level=True)
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.usefixtures("dist_init")
+
+HIDDEN = 256
+D, W = 128, 4
+NUM_SLOTS = 24
+PREFIX = "model.layers.0.self_attn"
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def model_dir(tmp_path_factory) -> str:
+    """A one-layer GLM-5.3-Flash config; the layer needs no checkpoint."""
+    path = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("glm5next")
+    config = Glm5NextTextConfig(
+        hidden_size=HIDDEN, num_hidden_layers=1, layer_types=["linear_attention"]
+    )
+    config.architectures = ["Glm5NextForCausalLM"]
+    config.save_pretrained(path)
+    return str(path)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def conv_state_layout(request, monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT", request.param)
+    get_conv_state_layout.cache_clear()
+    yield request.param
+    get_conv_state_layout.cache_clear()
+
+
+def _make_layer(
+    model_dir: str,
+    num_heads: int,
+    decode: str = "triton",
+    prefill: str = "triton",
+    num_spec: int = 0,
+    state_dtype: torch.dtype = torch.float32,
+) -> tuple[Glm5NextLinearAttention, VllmConfig]:
+    """A layer with seeded weights and caches, post-processed as after a load."""
+    vllm_config = create_vllm_config(
+        model_name=model_dir,
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        hf_config_override={"linear_num_heads": num_heads},
+    )
+    vllm_config.cache_config.mamba_ssm_cache_dtype = (
+        "float32" if state_dtype == torch.float32 else "bfloat16"
+    )
+    vllm_config.additional_config = {
+        "kda_decode_backend": decode,
+        "kda_spec_decode_backend": decode,
+        "kda_prefill_backend": prefill,
+    }
+    if num_spec:
+        vllm_config.speculative_config = SpeculativeConfig(
+            method="ngram", num_speculative_tokens=num_spec
+        )
+    with (
+        set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config),
+        set_default_torch_dtype(torch.bfloat16),
+        torch.device("cuda"),
+    ):
+        layer = Glm5NextLinearAttention(
+            vllm_config.model_config.hf_text_config, vllm_config, PREFIX
+        )
+
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0)
+    for param in layer.parameters():
+        weight = torch.randn(param.shape, device="cuda", generator=g)
+        default_weight_loader(param, weight / param.shape[-1] ** 0.5)
+    heads = torch.linspace(1, 16, layer.local_num_heads, device="cuda")
+    default_weight_loader(layer.A_log, heads.log().view_as(layer.A_log))
+    layer.o_norm.weight.data.add_(1)
+    layer.process_weights_after_loading()
+
+    shapes, dtypes = layer.get_state_shape(), layer.get_state_dtype()
+    page_bytes = sum(prod(s) * d.itemsize for s, d in zip(shapes, dtypes))
+    layer.bind_kv_cache(
+        torch.zeros(NUM_SLOTS, 1, 1, page_bytes, dtype=torch.int8, device="cuda")
+    )
+    for cache, scale in zip(layer.kv_cache, (1.0, 0.2)):
+        cache.copy_(scale * torch.randn(cache.shape, device="cuda", generator=g))
+    return layer, vllm_config
+
+
+def _require_flashinfer_decode(layer: Glm5NextLinearAttention) -> None:
+    backend = (
+        layer.kda_spec_decode_backend if layer.num_spec else layer.kda_decode_backend
+    )
+    if backend != "flashinfer":
+        pytest.skip("FlashInfer fused KDA decode does not support this config")
+
+
+def _require_flashinfer_prefill(state_dtype: torch.dtype) -> None:
+    if not _is_flashinfer_kda_prefill_supported(D, torch.bfloat16, state_dtype, -5.0):
+        pytest.skip("FlashInfer KDA prefill does not support this platform")
+
+
+def _hidden(num_tokens: int, seed: int = 1) -> torch.Tensor:
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    return torch.randn(num_tokens, HIDDEN, device="cuda", generator=g).bfloat16()
+
+
+def _forward(
+    layer: Glm5NextLinearAttention,
+    vllm_config: VllmConfig,
+    meta: GDNAttentionMetadata,
+    hidden: torch.Tensor,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    positions = torch.arange(hidden.size(0), device="cuda")
+    with (
+        set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config),
+        set_forward_context({PREFIX: meta}, vllm_config),
+    ):
+        return layer(hidden, positions)
+
+
+def _non_spec_metadata(
+    query_lens: list[int],
+    num_decodes: int,
+    slots: list[int],
+    has_state: list[bool],
+    block_table_width: int = 1,
+) -> GDNAttentionMetadata:
+    """Non-spec metadata as the builder makes it: decodes first, then the
+    prefill tail rebased for the peeled path. The slot indices are column 0
+    of a [N, block_table_width] block table (1 + num_spec columns with
+    speculative decoding, so a strided view)."""
+    qsl_cpu = torch.tensor([0, *torch.tensor(query_lens).cumsum(0).tolist()]).int()
+    qsl = qsl_cpu.cuda()
+    block_table = torch.zeros(
+        len(slots), block_table_width, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"
+    )
+    block_table[:, 0] = torch.tensor(slots, dtype=torch.int32)
+    indices = block_table[:, 0]
+    has_initial_state = torch.tensor(has_state, device="cuda")
+    num_tokens = int(qsl_cpu[-1])
+    prefill: dict[str, Any] = {}
+    if num_decodes < len(query_lens):
+        nums_dict, batch_ptr, token_chunk_offset_ptr = compute_causal_conv1d_metadata(
+            qsl_cpu, device=qsl.device
+        )
+        prefill = dict(
+            has_initial_state=has_initial_state,
+            nums_dict=nums_dict,
+            batch_ptr=batch_ptr,
+            token_chunk_offset_ptr=token_chunk_offset_ptr,
+            prefill_query_start_loc=qsl[num_decodes:] - num_decodes,
+            prefill_state_indices=indices[num_decodes:],
+            prefill_has_initial_state=has_initial_state[num_decodes:],
+        )
+    return GDNAttentionMetadata(
+        num_prefills=len(query_lens) - num_decodes,
+        num_prefill_tokens=num_tokens - num_decodes,
+        num_decodes=num_decodes,
+        num_decode_tokens=num_decodes,
+        num_spec_decodes=0,
+        num_spec_decode_tokens=0,
+        num_actual_tokens=num_tokens,
+        non_spec_query_start_loc=qsl,
+        non_spec_state_indices_tensor=indices,
+        **prefill,
+    )
+
+
+def _spec_metadata(
+    num_spec: int,
+    accepted: list[int],
+    prefill_lens: list[int],
+    slots: list[list[int]],
+) -> GDNAttentionMetadata:
+    """Draft-verify rows first (1 + num_spec tokens each), then prefills."""
+    T = 1 + num_spec
+    num_spec_rows = len(accepted)
+    lens = [T] * num_spec_rows + prefill_lens
+    is_spec = torch.tensor([1] * num_spec_rows + [0] * len(prefill_lens)).bool()
+    token_is_spec = torch.repeat_interleave(is_spec, torch.tensor(lens))
+    prefill: dict[str, Any] = {}
+    if prefill_lens:
+        qsl_cpu = torch.tensor(
+            [0, *torch.tensor(prefill_lens).cumsum(0).tolist()]
+        ).int()
+        qsl = qsl_cpu.cuda()
+        indices = torch.tensor(
+            [s[0] for s in slots[num_spec_rows:]], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"
+        )
+        has_initial_state = torch.tensor([False, True], device="cuda")[
+            : len(prefill_lens)
+        ]
+        nums_dict, batch_ptr, token_chunk_offset_ptr = compute_causal_conv1d_metadata(
+            qsl_cpu, device=qsl.device
+        )
+        prefill = dict(
+            non_spec_query_start_loc=qsl,
+            non_spec_state_indices_tensor=indices,
+            has_initial_state=has_initial_state,
+            nums_dict=nums_dict,
+            batch_ptr=batch_ptr,
+            token_chunk_offset_ptr=token_chunk_offset_ptr,
+            prefill_query_start_loc=qsl,
+            prefill_state_indices=indices,
+            prefill_has_initial_state=has_initial_state,
+        )
+    return GDNAttentionMetadata(
+        num_prefills=len(prefill_lens),
+        num_prefill_tokens=sum(prefill_lens),
+        num_decodes=0,
+        num_decode_tokens=0,
+        num_spec_decodes=num_spec_rows,
+        num_spec_decode_tokens=T * num_spec_rows,
+        num_actual_tokens=sum(lens),
+        spec_query_start_loc=torch.arange(
+            0, T * num_spec_rows + 1, T, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"
+        ),
+        spec_state_indices_tensor=torch.tensor(
+            slots[:num_spec_rows], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"
+        ),
+        spec_sequence_masks=is_spec.cuda(),
+        spec_token_indx=token_is_spec.nonzero().flatten().cuda(),
+        non_spec_token_indx=(~token_is_spec).nonzero().flatten().cuda(),
+        num_accepted_tokens=torch.tensor(accepted, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
+        **prefill,
+    )
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_backend_selection(model_dir):
+    """``auto`` runs GLM-5.3's decode shapes (64 heads at TP1, 16 at TP4) on
+    FlashInfer on SM10x, keeps Triton for 8-head draft-verify rows, and an
+    explicit ``flashinfer`` fails at startup where it is unsupported."""
+    if not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100):
+        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="SM10x"):
+            _make_layer(model_dir, 64, decode="flashinfer")
+        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="SM100/SM103/SM107"):
+            _make_layer(model_dir, 64, prefill="flashinfer")
+        return
+    for num_heads in (16, 64):
+        layer, _ = _make_layer(model_dir, num_heads, decode="auto")
+        assert layer.kda_decode_backend == "flashinfer"
+        layer, _ = _make_layer(model_dir, num_heads, decode="auto", num_spec=2)
+        assert layer.kda_spec_decode_backend == "flashinfer"
+    layer, _ = _make_layer(model_dir, 8, decode="auto", num_spec=2)
+    assert layer.kda_spec_decode_backend == "triton"
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="SM10x"):
+        _make_layer(model_dir, 8, decode="flashinfer", num_spec=2)
+    layer, _ = _make_layer(model_dir, 64, prefill="flashinfer")
+    assert layer.kda_prefill_backend == "flashinfer"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("conv_state_layout", ["SD", "DS"], indirect=True)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "state_dtype", [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16], ids=["fp32", "bf16"]
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_heads", [16, 64])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_decode_step_matches_triton(
+    model_dir, num_heads, state_dtype, conv_state_layout
+):
+    flashinfer = _make_layer(model_dir, num_heads, "auto", state_dtype=state_dtype)
+    _require_flashinfer_decode(flashinfer[0])
+    triton = _make_layer(model_dir, num_heads, state_dtype=state_dtype)
+    before = [cache.clone() for cache in triton[0].kv_cache]
+    # Null rows (slot 0, also CUDA-graph padding) must not touch any cache.
+    slots = [3, 0, 7, 11, 0, 19, 1, 22]
+    meta = _non_spec_metadata([1] * len(slots), len(slots), slots, [True] * 8)
+    hidden = _hidden(len(slots))
+    out_t = _forward(*triton, meta, hidden)
+    out_f = _forward(*flashinfer, meta, hidden)
+
+    (conv_t, state_t), (conv_f, state_f) = triton[0].kv_cache, flashinfer[0].kv_cache
+    torch.testing.assert_close(conv_f, conv_t, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    tol = 2e-2 if state_dtype == torch.bfloat16 else 2e-3
+    torch.testing.assert_close(state_f, state_t, atol=tol, rtol=tol)
+    live = torch.tensor(slots) > 0
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out_f[live], out_t[live], atol=3e-2, rtol=3e-2)
+    untouched = [s for s in range(NUM_SLOTS) if s not in slots or s == 0]
+    for cache, original in zip(flashinfer[0].kv_cache, before):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            cache[untouched], original[untouched], atol=0, rtol=0
+        )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("prefill", ["triton", "flashkda", "flashinfer"])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_mixed_step_matches_triton(model_dir, workspace_init, prefill):
+    """The decode rows of a mixed step go through the fused decode; the
+    prefill rows (fresh and continued) and their states do not change."""
+    num_heads = 16
